context.issue:
Issue #181133: [MPS] scaled_dot_product_attention returns wrong values for non-contiguous (permute-produced) q/k/v
## 🐛 Describe the bug

On MPS, `F.scaled_dot_product_attention` returns numerically incorrect results when given non-contiguous tensors produced by `permute(0, 2, 1, 3)`. Inserting `.contiguous()` after the permute restores correct output.

Distinct from #179352, which requires total elements > 2³². This fires at tiny shapes (~5M elements).

### Minimal reproduction

```python
import torch

assert torch.backends.mps.is_available()
torch.manual_seed(0)

B, S, H, D = 84, 3, 3, 64
q = torch.randn(B, S, H, D)
k = torch.randn(B, S, H, D)
v = torch.randn(B, S, H, D)


def call(q, k, v, make_contiguous: bool):
    q = q.permute(0, 2, 1, 3)
    k = k.permute(0, 2, 1, 3)
    v = v.permute(0, 2, 1, 3)
    if make_contiguous:
        q, k, v = q.contiguous(), k.contiguous(), v.contiguous()
    return torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v)


for mk in (False, True):
    o_cpu = call(q, k, v, mk)
    o_mps = call(q.to("mps"), k.to("mps"), v.to("mps"), mk).cpu()
    print(f"contiguous={mk}: max abs err = {(o_cpu - o_mps).abs().max().item():.4g}")
```

```
contiguous=False: max abs err = 3.618
contiguous=True:  max abs err = 7.749e-07
```

### Bug regime (from a dimension sweep)

Triggers when all of:
- \`head_dim ≥ 64\`
- \`seq_len ∈ [2, 8]\` (works at \`S=1\`; works again at \`S ≥ 16\`)
- \`batch ≥ 2\`

Smaller \`head_dim\` or outside this sequence-length band produces correct output with the same permute pattern.

### Workaround

\`.contiguous()\` after the permute before calling SDPA.

### Versions

- \`torch==2.11.0\`
- macOS 26.3.1 / arm64

### Related

- #179352 — large batch × seq case (different regime, same op/backend)
- #179294 — MPS SDPA improvements umbrella

messages.minimax:
fix[MPS]: add batch stride handling to SDPA kernels for permuted inputs

Fixes #181133

The MPS SDPA kernels incorrectly computed tensor offsets when q/k/v tensors were non-contiguous (e.g., produced by permute(0, 2, 1, 3)). The kernels only tracked head and sequence strides but not batch strides, causing batch elements to alias into each other.

This change:
- Adds a `qkv_batch_strides_heads` buffer containing batch strides for q/k/v and num_heads
- Derives batch_idx and head_idx from thread ID instead of assuming contiguous batch×num_heads layout
- Simplifies the contiguous check in the caller to only require stride(-1) == 1 since the kernels now handle arbitrary strides
- Adds a regression test for the permuted-input case
messages.claude:
feat: support non-contiguous strides in MPS SDPA fast path

Fixes #181133.

Previously, the MPS SDPA vector kernels derived q/k/v offsets solely from head and sequence strides, implicitly assuming the batch dimension was contiguous (strides[0] == strides[2] * sizes[2]). When callers passed tensors produced via permute(0, 2, 1, 3), the batch stride no longer matched this assumption, so the kernels read from incorrect memory and returned numerically wrong results at small shapes (batch >= 2, seq_len in [2, 8], head_dim >= 64). The host-side gate further forced a .contiguous() copy unless the tensor matched a narrow "contiguous or head-seq transposed" layout, hiding the kernel limitation but paying an extra copy and still miscompiling offsets for genuinely transposed inputs.

This change threads explicit batch strides (and num_heads) into the Metal kernels via a new qkv_batch_strides_heads constant buffer, and rewrites the pointer arithmetic in sdpa_vector and sdpa_vector_2pass_1 to index batch_idx = bh_idx / num_heads and head_idx = bh_idx % num_heads, adding batch_idx * {q,k,v}_batch_stride to every base pointer. Mask indexing is likewise switched to the flattened bh_idx so it stays aligned with the new batch*head dispatch.

On the host side, the contiguity gate is relaxed to t.stride(-1) == 1, since the kernels now load head-dim elements linearly and only require the innermost stride to be unit. This lets permuted-but-unit-stride tensors skip the .contiguous() copy while producing correct output.

Adds test_fast_vector_permuted_inputs_regression as a regression test for issue #181133.
messages.kimi:
[MPS] Fix SDPA returning wrong values for non-contiguous permuted inputs (#181133)

The fast SDPA kernels were not correctly handling non-contiguous tensors
produced by operations like permute(0, 2, 1, 3). The kernels assumed
contiguous batch strides when computing memory offsets, leading to
incorrect results when Q/K/V tensors had non-standard layouts.

This fix:
- Adds batch stride parameters (qkv_batch_strides_heads) to the Metal
  kernels to properly compute memory offsets per batch
- Updates the kernel dispatch logic to extract batch indices and apply
  correct stride offsets for queries, keys, and values
- Relaxes the contiguity requirement from full contiguity to only
  requiring stride(-1) == 1 (head-dim contiguous), avoiding unnecessary
  copies

Fixes #181133

messages.claude:
feat: Add CUDA 12.9 binary builds for PyTorch 2.12

https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/185269

Adds CUDA 12.9 to the binary build matrix for nightly and stable
release pipelines, including x86_64 and aarch64 Linux manywheel builds
across Python 3.10–3.14 (plus 3.14t), libtorch shared-with-deps
artifacts, and the corresponding docker image tags (almalinux and
manylinux2_28 builders).

CUDA 12.9 is intentionally limited to Linux for both x86_64 and aarch64
because the underlying CUDA toolkit and driver stack for Windows is not
being published for this version; the wheels/libtorch matrix generator
explicitly filters 12.9 out of the Windows CUDA arch list via
list_without.

The PYTORCH_EXTRA_INSTALL_REQUIREMENTS for cu129 pin the cuda-toolkit
metapackage to 12.9.1, cuda-bindings to >=12.9.4,<13, cudnn to
9.20.0.48, cusparselt to 0.8.1, nccl to 2.29.7, and nvshmem to 3.4.5,
matching the runtime dependency set shipped with the CUDA 12.9 SDK.

This unblocks downstream consumers — most notably SGLang — who depend on
the PyTorch 2.11 cu129 binary and are not yet ready to migrate to
cu130 in the 2.12 release. Providing a 2.12 cu129 binary gives them
one additional release cycle to transition to cu130, as requested in the
issue.

Pull Request resolved: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/185269
Approved by: @malfet @atalman

messages.claude:
ci: disambiguate Windows arm64 libtorch packages from x86_64

Windows x86_64 and arm64 libtorch builds produced artifacts with
identical filenames (e.g. libtorch-win-shared-with-deps) and job names
(libtorch-cpu-shared-with-deps-release), causing the arm64 upload to
overwrite the x86_64 package in the upload bucket. As reported in
issue #187812, the published 2.12.1 Windows release shipped arm64
binaries in place of the expected x64 package — `file libtorch/lib/c10.dll`
returned `PE32+ ... Aarch64` instead of x86_64.

Add an --arch argument to extract_libtorch_from_wheel.py and thread it
through compute_zip_prefix and generate_libtorch_extraction_configs so
arm64 builds get a libtorch-win-arm64-* prefix and a libtorch-arm64-*
build_name. The Windows binary build workflow template and the generated
x86_64/arm64 nightly workflows pass the appropriate --arch value, and
the arm64 extract/upload job names are renamed accordingly.

Pull Request resolved: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/187813
Approved by: https://github.com/malfet
messages.kimi:
ci: Disambiguate Windows x86_64 and arm64 libtorch package names to prevent upload collisions

The Windows x86_64 and arm64 libtorch packages were sharing the same filename (e.g., `libtorch-cpu-shared-with-deps-release`), causing the arm64 build to overwrite the x86_64 build in the upload bucket. This resulted in users downloading the wrong architecture binary (Issue #187812).

Add `--arch` parameter to `extract_libtorch_from_wheel.py` and include architecture in build names and zip prefixes for Windows builds. This ensures x86_64 and arm64 packages have distinct names and can coexist in the artifact storage.
messages.minimax:
fix: include architecture in Windows libtorch package names to prevent overwrite

On Windows, libtorch x86_64 and arm64 packages shared the same filename
(e.g. libtorch-cpu-shared-with-deps-release), causing them to overwrite each
other in the upload bucket. This was reported in issue #187812 where the
release prebuilt was incorrectly ARM when users expected X64.

Changes:
- Add --arch flag to extract_libtorch_from_wheel.py and compute_zip_prefix()
- Include arch in build name for windows-arm64 (libtorch-arm64-{variant}-...)
- Update generated workflow templates and nightly workflows to pass --arch

This ensures x86_64 and arm64 packages have distinct names and don't collide
